messages:

Subject: Data residency & DPA annex for PayFlux integration

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — PayFlux product team is moving quickly and we need to close a few legal/technical items before we can start the pilot. Can you help with the following?

1) DPA annex: we sent a redline (attached) — are you able to confirm whether Redwood can commit to the residency carveouts in section 4.2 for tokenized payment metadata?

2) Subprocessor roster & roles: we need the full roster of subprocessors that will process cardholder metadata or any unredacted PII, plus a high-level role (processing/hosting/monitoring).

3) Dataflow diagram: can you provide an updated dataflow that shows where PII is persisted vs transient (KV cache, long-term store, analytics)? We need to show control points for PCI/Privacy review.

4) KMS custody options: will Redwood accept a customer-managed key for token encryption, or do we need an escrow option for the pilot?

We'd like this information in the next 5 business days if possible. Attachments: PayFlux_DPA_redline_v1.docx (see comments).

Best,
Sam
Sam Reynolds
Head of Integrations | PayFlux

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rohan (infra/security) and Kimberly (privacy) to scope the answers and pull artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Residency carveouts: we can commit to a residency boundary for persisted payment metadata for US-only processing under the pilot, subject to DPA annex language and an agreed exception for autoscaling transient nodes.
- Subprocessor roster: we'll provide the current roster and mark which subprocessors touch unredacted PII.
- Dataflow diagram: will share an annotated diagram showing KV cache vs durable storage.
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported for long-term storage; for KV cache we'll propose a split custody/escrow workflow for the pilot.

Next steps: Rohan/Kimberly — can you prepare the annotated dataflow + roster and a short note on the KMS custody options? Sam — if you can share the redline link and any compliance checklist items (PCI scoping, SOC2 artifacts needed), we'll map them to artifacts.

Thanks,

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & DPA annex for PayFlux integration (internal technical details)

Marissa / Kimberly — drafting the artifacts now. Key technical points to be explicit about in our response to PayFlux:

- Processing zones: we separate request plane (edge ingress), inference runtime (GPU pools), and durable store (object storage). PII persists only in the durable store when explicitly configured by the customer. Transient KV cache lives in the runtime but is memory-only and evicted on policy.

- Tokenization/pseudonymization: For payment metadata we recommend tokenization at ingestion (customer-side) where PayFlux can either:
  * Use customer-managed keys (CMK) for long-term token storage in object store (supported), or
  * For pilot, allow Redwood-provided ephemeral tokens with split-key escrow — keys are split between Redwood HSM and an escrow service (approved subprocessors) and never exported in clear.

- Subprocessor impact: attached roster marks subprocessors that access object storage (S3), monitoring (Datadog), and build/ops (GitHub Actions). Only three subprocessors have potential access to unredacted PII in normal operations; those are covered by our subprocessors' SOC2 attestations and contractual clauses.

- Proof artifacts: we'll attach
  1) annotated dataflow (dataflow_paymentflows_v2.pdf) — highlights persist vs transient, egress points, and KMS boundaries.
  2) subprocessor_roster_2028-07.csv — exported with role tags and SOC2 expiry dates.
  3) short KMS custody note (inline below).

KMS custody options (short):
- Option A (Preferred): Customer-managed KMS for object store. Redwood integrates via KMS API; keys never leave the customer KMS.
- Option B (Pilot Escrow): Split-key escrow for transient cache — Redwood holds HSM shard 1, escrow provider shard 2; no single party can reconstruct without both shards.
- Option C: Redwood-managed keys with strict access controls & audit logs (fallback only).

I'll attach the artifacts and a one-page diagram for Kimberly to review before we send to PayFlux.

Attachments: dataflow_paymentflows_v2.pdf, subprocessor_roster_2028-07.csv

-Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sam / Jill — thanks for the patience. Attached are the materials requested for your compliance review:

- PayFlux_DPA_annotated_v1.docx (we accepted a few of your language requests and flagged two items for legal: section 4.2 residency carveout wording and appendix B liability cap language)
- dataflow_paymentflows_v2.pdf (annotated: persisted vs transient, KV cache eviction policy, egress control points)
- subprocessor_roster_2028-07.csv (roles + SOC2 expiry)

Summary of commitments for the pilot:
- Residency: Redwood will ensure persisted payment metadata for the PayFlux pilot is stored in US regions only. Transient compute nodes may briefly spin up in other regions for autoscaling; those nodes do not persist PII and are subject to our KV eviction policy.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS supported for object store (Option A). For KV cache we propose the split-key escrow pilot (Option B) — details in the attached KMS note.
- Subprocessors: only three subprocessors have path to unredacted PII; SOC2 reports are available on request.

Please review the attached annotated DPA and let us know:
1) Are the two flagged legal items acceptable to PayFlux counsel for the pilot?
2) Do you need SOC2 PDFs or do the roster + expiry fields suffice for initial review?

Next steps: If the pilot terms look good, Marissa will get DocuSign prepared for the DPA annex and Rohan will configure the pilot environment with CMK + escrow as agreed.

Thanks and happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd like to walk through the diagram.

Best,
